transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee is putting a hold on capital punishment in the state until
investigators determine what led to the botched execution of death row inmate Christa Gail
Pike yesterday.
So far as we know, the Department of Corrections followed exactly the protocol that was outlined
and vetted and approved by the Attorney General's office.
At this point, that is all we know.
Pike, who was 18 when she was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, was heard snoring
loudly after receiving two lethal injections.
She was taken by ambulance to the hospital.
Lawyers filed an emergency motion to the Supreme Court to stay the execution, saying Pike was
in unnecessary agony and that her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment
was being violated.
It was a second time this year that Tennessee has been unable to carry out an execution.
And Trump is expected to tout recent initiatives as he campaigns today for Republican congressional
candidates.
St. Pierre's Frank Ordonea says one stop is Oklahoma.
It's certainly a place where he can get an enthusiastic response to this week's announcements
for, for example, a $15 billion steel plant being built in Iowa, as well as a $54 billion
investment by South Korea into a project to export natural gas from Alaska.
And both of those are battleground states.
Trump's also going to Texas, Vice President J.D. Vance will be in Florida.
Egg prices have fallen dramatically since early last year.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports, agriculture experts say much of that decline in prices
has to do with avian flu.
An outbreak of avian flu that started in late 2024 was so severe that it resulted in the
deaths of more than 50 million egg laying hens in just six months.
The hit to the U.S. poultry supply caused egg prices to rise.
But since then, farms have been able to rebuild their flocks and they've enhanced their biosecurity
protections with help from the Trump administration.
Poultry industry analysts say those efforts, plus a more recent milder avian flu season,
have caused prices to drop again.
In August, egg prices were down 23 percent year over year, yet eggs were an exception.
Overall grocery prices had increased by 2.2 percent.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
The administration made some last minute changes to the forms used by U.S. citizens who cast
ballots from outside the U.S.
Many overseas and military voters used two absentee voting forms that are overseen by
the Pentagon.
In August, the Trump administration made an emergency request to remove a long-standing
category for U.S. citizens who were born abroad and have never lived in the United States.
And sometimes because their U.S. citizen parents or legal guardians served overseas in the
U.S. military.
Many states allowed these citizens to vote if a parent last lived or was registered to
vote there before leaving the country.
The Pentagon says it now believes those overseas citizens are not eligible to use its forms,
but that state election officials can continue processing older versions of the forms.
Hansi Lo Wang reporting, it's NPR News.
Egyptian security forces have arrested six journalists working for an independent online
Arabic news outlet.
The sweep targets the news organization's entire editorial team, who have yet to face
formal charges.
We have the latest from NPR's Eya Betrawi.
The six male journalists were arrested in raids on their homes in different parts of Egypt
this week.
They all work for an independent news outlet called Metsa Desh, which translates to "don't
believe."
The outlet was launched in 2018 and specializes in fact-checking.
It says it has no affiliation to any political party.
The group's interior ministry says the news outlet is unlicensed and has broadcast false
news and distorted facts.
It says an examination revealed that the website is linked to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood
group and managed by one of its figures in exile abroad.
The ministry provided no evidence to support this accusation.
The Committee to Protect Journalists and other rights groups issued a joint statement saying
the arrests mark an alarming escalation against independent media that cannot be allowed to
stand.
Eya Betrawi, NPR News.
In Pennsylvania, health officials are confirming a fifth death related to measles.
The patient lived in Lancaster County, which is the epicenter of the state's measles outbreak.
SpaceX sent four astronauts to the International Space Station today.
The team will live on the orbiting outpost until next spring.
Dr. Jessica Watkins has become the first black woman to lead a crew to orbit, but it is her
second trip to the space station.
The geologists also worked with NASA's Mars Rover Curiosity a decade ago.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee halts capital punishment after botched execution of Christa Gail Pike
Trump campaigns for Republican congressional candidates with announcements of major industrial investments
Egg prices fall dramatically since early 2024 due to avian flu recovery and biosecurity improvements
Trump administration removes citizenship category from overseas military voter absentee ballot forms
Egyptian security forces arrest six journalists from independent fact-checking news outlet Metsa Desh
Pennsylvania health officials confirm fifth death related to measles in Lancaster County outbreak
SpaceX sends four astronauts to International Space Station with Dr. Jessica Watkins leading crew
